title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: section 9-10 of the notes on the 'structure at infinity' of the moduli stacks M_{g,ν}. Grothendieck is axiomatizing, in purely combinatorial and groupoid terms, the homotopy type of the Deligne-Mumford compactification near its boundary.

The data are as follows.
- There is a category 𝒢 of 'MD-graphs' (Mumford-Deligne dual graphs of stable curves).
- Its morphisms are isomorphisms and 'generalization' morphisms G → G' = G/C. Here C ⊂ A_G is a set of edges (double points) that are smoothed, and G/C is the quotient attached to A_G∖C, i.e. the graph keeping the remaining nodes. Condition (Simpl), on the previous page, says that the poset of quotients of G is the power set of the finite set A_G.
- To each G are attached two groupoids. ΠM_G is the fundamental groupoid of the open stratum M_G. SΠM_G is the fundamental groupoid of the punctured tubular neighbourhood, i.e. the link torus bundle of the stratum.
- There is a map φ_G: SΠM_G → ΠM_G making SΠM_G an extension of ΠM_G by Z^{A(G)}. The generators are the local monodromies (Dehn twists) around the branches of the normal-crossings boundary divisor through the stratum.

On this page:
- G ↦ ΠM_G is required to be functorial for isomorphisms.
- G ↦ SΠM_G is required to be functorial for all morphisms, including generalizations (the deeper tube maps into the shallower one).
- φ_G is required to be natural for isomorphisms.
- For a generalization f: G → G/C, the composite SΠM_G → SΠM_{G'} → ΠM_{G'} must factor through S_C M_G. This is the extension of ΠM_G by Z^C obtained by pushing out SΠM_G along the projection Z^{A(G)} → Z^C. It yields a map r_f: S_C M_G → ΠM_{G'} (diagram (125)).

Geometric meaning: twists around nodes that persist in G' lie in the kernel of φ_{G'} and die. Twists around the smoothed nodes in C survive as genuine Dehn twists in π_1 of the less degenerate stratum. Since S_C M_G is a quotient of SΠM_G, the factorization is unique when it exists. Transitivity for composites G → G' → G'' therefore follows automatically, as Grothendieck notes.

The purpose is a discrete 'MDT structure': an abstract system of groupoids indexed by the stratification poset, from which the Teichmüller tower and its boundary gluing can be studied. The next page extends this to normalization morphisms, i.e. maps M_G → M_{g_α, Î_α}.
errors: In diagram (125) the left vertical arrow is labelled φ_G but points to S_C M_G. It should be the canonical projection SΠM_G → S_C M_G (the pushout along Z^{A(G)} → Z^C); φ_G itself goes to ΠM_G. This is a notational slip.

Compatibility is not stated explicitly. One needs SΠ(f) to send the subgroup Z^{A(G)∖C} into the kernel Z^{A(G')} of φ_{G'} (identifying A(G') with A(G)∖C), and the Z^C part to map injectively. The marginal NB on the previous page signals awareness that further structure is needed.
The direction convention for G/C (quotient attached to A_G∖C, 'smaller as C is larger') is consistent with C being the set of smoothed nodes, but the wording is convoluted.

ideas.what: Boundary strata of M̄_{g,n} described by a fundamental groupoid of the stratum plus a Z^{nodes} extension (the link torus bundle / local monodromy by Dehn twists)
ideas.modern_name: Local monodromy at normal-crossings boundary; log fundamental group of a log stratum (Kato-Nakayama torus bundle)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Deligne, SGA7-style local monodromy); log version Kato-Nakayama, Illusie; for M_{g,n}: Ihara-Nakamura, Nakamura, Boggi
ideas.where_published: Spirit present in Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, 'tubular neighbourhoods' at infinity), not in this axiomatic form

ideas.what: Poset-indexed system of groupoid extensions with functoriality for generalizations and factorization through pushouts Z^{A}→Z^{C}
ideas.modern_name: Stratified fundamental groupoid / exit-path category of the DM stratification; combinatorial 'Lego' presentation of Teichmüller groupoids
ideas.usually_credited_to: MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie (exit paths); Bakalov-Kirillov, Hatcher-Lochak-Schneps, Moore-Seiberg (Lego-Teichmüller game)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme sketches the Lego-Teichmüller game; this formal axiomatization is unsure

ideas.what: Uniqueness of the factorization implying automatic transitivity for composites
ideas.modern_name: Coherence of a lax functor by uniqueness of factorization through quotients

missed.claim: The axiom (a Z^{A(G)} extension over each stratum, with specialization maps factoring through the pushout to Z^C for the smoothed nodes) is a purely combinatorial precursor of the Kato-Nakayama / logarithmic fundamental groupoid of the log stack M̄_{g,n}. There the factorization through N^A → N^C is built into the log structure. Grothendieck frames it as an axiomatic 'discrete MDT structure' indexed by the stratification poset, i.e. an exit-path-type description.
missed.quote: se factorise par l'extension S_C M_G de ΠM_G par Z^C, déduite de l'extension SΠM_G de ΠM_G par Z^{A(G)} grâce à l'homom canonique Z^{A(G)}→Z^C
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Abstract axiomatizations of the 'boundary groupoid' of M̄_{g,n} appear only piecemeal in the literature (Boggi, Nakamura, Hatcher-Lochak-Schneps). The notes may contain a fuller axiomatic framework, of interest for anabelian approaches to the Grothendieck-Teichmüller group acting on the tower with its boundary. The idea itself is not new.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful unpublished axiomatization of the tubular/boundary groupoid structure of the Deligne-Mumford stratification. The ingredients (local monodromy Z^{nodes}, Dehn twists, specialization) are well known, and the Lego-Teichmüller philosophy is in the Esquisse. The precise combinatorial-groupoid axiom system is a notable but unsurprising detail.
transcription_corrections: In diagram (125) the bottom-left object is written S_C M_G with a crossed-out letter under the subscript. The left arrow label φ_G is as written but is mathematically the projection.
'telle que G→G' soit isom, ou que quotient de G, à G→G/C' reads more plausibly as 'telle que G→G' soit isom au quotient de G, i.e. à G→G/C'.
'it que le composé' should read 'i.e. que le composé'.
